turns.speaker: Agent
turns.text: Hi there, this is Arjun calling from Acme Life. I'm returning a call-back request about our term life insurance. Just so you know, this call is recorded for quality and training purposes.

turns.speaker: Customer
turns.text: Oh, hi. Yes, I filled out that form on your website a couple of days ago.

turns.speaker: Agent
turns.text: Perfect. I've got it up here. So it's Emma Wong, you're fifty-four, non-smoker, living in Mississauga, and you were looking at around a hundred and fifty thousand dollars of cover. The online estimate came out at about thirty-three dollars a month for a ten-year term. Does that all still sound right?

turns.speaker: Customer
turns.text: Yes, that's what I put in. I wasn't sure if that number was real or just a teaser.

turns.speaker: Agent
turns.text: Fair question. It's a genuine estimate based on what you entered, but the final price does depend on a few health questions. Before we get into that, can I ask what got you thinking about life insurance right now?

turns.speaker: Customer
turns.text: Well, honestly, I went to my doctor last month and found out I have high blood pressure. It kind of shook me. My husband and I still have about ten years left on the mortgage, and I just started worrying about what happens if something happens to me.

turns.speaker: Agent
turns.text: That makes complete sense, and a lot of people come to us after a moment like that. Do you have anyone else depending on your income, kids at home, anything like that?

turns.speaker: Customer
turns.text: Our daughter's at university, so we're helping with tuition for another two years. Our son's finished school and working. Mainly it's the mortgage and my husband. My income covers about half the household bills.

turns.speaker: Agent
turns.text: Okay. And roughly how much is left on the mortgage?

turns.speaker: Customer
turns.text: About a hundred and twenty thousand, give or take.

turns.speaker: Agent
turns.text: And do you have any coverage already, maybe through work?

turns.speaker: Customer
turns.text: There's a small group plan through my employer, I think it's one times my salary, but if I leave the job it goes away, so I don't want to rely on it.

turns.speaker: Agent
turns.text: Good thinking. Based on what you've told me, the hundred and fifty thousand over ten years lines up quite well. It would cover the remaining mortgage with some left over for your husband and your daughter's tuition, and the term matches the time left on the mortgage. We do offer anywhere from fifty thousand up to seven hundred and fifty thousand, and terms of either ten or twenty years, so we can adjust if you'd like.

turns.speaker: Customer
turns.text: I did wonder about twenty years. Is that a lot more?

turns.speaker: Agent
turns.text: It would be more per month, since it covers you for longer and into your seventies. Whichever term you pick, the premium is fixed for the whole term, so it won't go up partway through. Given your main concern is the mortgage over the next ten years, ten years seems the better fit, but it's your call.

turns.speaker: Customer
turns.text: No, ten makes sense. Now, the blood pressure. Is that going to be a problem? I saw something about no medical exam.

turns.speaker: Agent
turns.text: Right, there's no medical exam. No needles, no nurse visit. Instead there are a few health questions, and acceptance depends on your answers. I can't promise the outcome before we go through them, but we can do them now and you'll know where you stand. Is that okay?

turns.speaker: Customer
turns.text: Sure, go ahead.

turns.speaker: Agent
turns.text: In the past five years, have you been diagnosed with or treated for heart disease, stroke, cancer, or kidney disease?

turns.speaker: Customer
turns.text: No, none of those.

turns.speaker: Agent
turns.text: Have you been diagnosed with high blood pressure, and if so, is it being treated?

turns.speaker: Customer
turns.text: Yes, diagnosed last month. My doctor put me on a low-dose medication, and I'm going back in six weeks to check it.

turns.speaker: Agent
turns.text: Thanks. And are you currently waiting on any tests, referrals to a specialist, or results?

turns.speaker: Customer
turns.text: Just the follow-up with my family doctor. No specialist.

turns.speaker: Agent
turns.text: Last one. In the past twelve months, have you used any tobacco or nicotine products?

turns.speaker: Customer
turns.text: No, never smoked.

turns.speaker: Agent
turns.text: Okay, I've entered those. Give me a second. Alright, you've been accepted, and the premium stays at thirty-three dollars a month for a hundred and fifty thousand over ten years. Treated high blood pressure with no other conditions didn't change the price here.

turns.speaker: Customer
turns.text: Oh, that's a relief. I was expecting worse. Can I ask, if I keep paying for ten years and nothing happens, do I get anything back?

turns.speaker: Agent
turns.text: No, and I want to be clear about that. It's pure term insurance, so there's no cash value and no money back at the end. That's partly why it's affordable. It pays the benefit to your beneficiary if you pass away during the term.

turns.speaker: Customer
turns.text: Hmm. I see. My sister has a policy that builds up money, I think.

turns.speaker: Agent
turns.text: That sounds like permanent insurance, which works differently and usually costs a lot more each month. If you'd like to think it over or compare, that's absolutely fine. The quote isn't going anywhere today, and you're welcome to talk it over with your husband first.

turns.speaker: Customer
turns.text: No, I think this is what I actually need. I just want the mortgage looked after. What if I sign up and then change my mind?

turns.speaker: Agent
turns.text: You'd have a thirty-day free-look period. If you cancel within thirty days of receiving the policy, you get a full refund of anything you've paid.

turns.speaker: Customer
turns.text: Okay, that makes me feel better. Let's do it.

turns.speaker: Agent
turns.text: Great. Before I finalize it, let me summarize. This is Acme Term Life, a hundred and fifty thousand dollars of coverage for a ten-year term, at thirty-three dollars a month, fixed for the full ten years. There's no cash value, and you have thirty days to cancel for a full refund. Would you like to go ahead with that?

turns.speaker: Customer
turns.text: Yes, I'd like to go ahead.

turns.speaker: Agent
turns.text: Wonderful. Who would you like to name as your beneficiary?

turns.speaker: Customer
turns.text: My husband, David Wong.

turns.speaker: Agent
turns.text: Got it. For payment, we can set up a monthly pre-authorized debit from your chequing account or put it on a credit card. Which do you prefer?

turns.speaker: Customer
turns.text: Pre-authorized debit from chequing is fine.

turns.speaker: Agent
turns.text: Perfect. I'll send you a secure link by email to enter your banking details, and your policy documents will follow within a couple of business days. The thirty days starts once you receive them.

turns.speaker: Customer
turns.text: Great. Thank you, Arjun, you've been really helpful.

turns.speaker: Agent
turns.text: My pleasure, Emma. Good luck with the follow-up appointment, and call us any time if you have questions. Have a great day.
